content.overview: Packaging is a controlled system made of material, closure, headspace, fill, handling and intended storage. Suitability must be demonstrated for the defined product and objective.

vocabulary.definition: Resistance of a package system to transfer of moisture, gases or light.
Combined package and closure components that protect and contain product.
Gas volume remaining inside a closed package around the product.

sections.title: The package is a system
sections.body: Film, jar, seal, liner, closure torque, fill and handling can all affect actual performance.

sections.title: Modified atmosphere is not universal protection
sections.body: Cannabis storage research found attribute-specific outcomes from nitrogen-modified atmosphere packaging, supporting measured validation rather than blanket claims.

sections.title: Compatibility includes moisture and chemical questions
sections.body: A package can limit one exposure while allowing another. Product condition and package permeability should be evaluated together over time.

workedExamples: A package reduces oxygen ingress but has an inconsistent closure; the material specification alone does not establish lot protection.
commonMistakes: Accepting supplier claims without product-specific evidence.
content.practicalApplication: Create a package-evidence matrix covering intended use, product condition, barrier claims, closure checks, handling and stability observations.
content.summary: Package suitability is an evidence question about the complete container-closure system in its real use.
